QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_38

question.text: Why do Category I and II AIFs find it difficult to use a broad-based listed-equity index (like Nifty 500 TR) as a direct benchmark?

answer.text: Cat I/II AIFs invest primarily in unlisted securities and early-stage start-ups with investment strategies that are thematic or sector-specific — there is no direct comparable listed index, hence PME/KS-PME adjustments are used.
SEBI prohibits Cat I/II AIFs from citing any listed index in any document.
Nifty 500 TR is a gross index and cannot be compared with any fund net return.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 7.5.1: 'Category I AIFs and Category II AIFs are investing in unlisted securities and early-stage start-ups. Hence, the investment managers cannot benchmark their performance against broad-based indices… one fund may have a thematic approach… another fund may have a sector-agnostic approach.' This is why PME / KS-PME / vintage-year benchmarks are used. The Trap: SEBI doesn't prohibit index citation (B). Nifty 500 TR is a total-return index — computed after dividends (C). D is factually wrong. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XIX-A test this conceptual gap. Contrast Cat III where broad indices are more usable (they trade listed securities). Manager's Pro-Tip: When LPs insist on a simple Nifty comparison, offer it as 'illustrative only' and pair with KS-PME / Direct Alpha which are pace-matched. Unadjusted Nifty vs illiquid fund comparison is analytically flawed and distorts track-record narratives.
